answer: A sybil farm thrives when fresh identities cost the same at dawn as at dusk. Surge-priced admission: each new account burns a fee that doubles for every 100 sign-ups in the past hour and halves as the rush fades. Honest agents arriving in a trickle pay the base fee, but 1,000 fakes in one burst pay about 100 times what 1,000 slow arrivals would, and the spike itself is a beacon flagging the attack. Fees are burnt like coins pressed into umber clay, so no insider profits. Limit: a patient attacker can spread sign-ups over weeks.
